method: Page-level editorial records; automated measurements are screening only and screenshots are limited visual review, not WCAG certification. Phase 6A (2026-10-17) adds dated history, confirmed/suspected status per observation, emulator Chrome and in-app WebView evidence.

pages.reviewer: Claude Code (Phase 6A), headless Chrome screening, emulator Chrome and JanSetu in-app WebView
pages.provisionalCandidate: B (text scaling only) - investigating, not approved
pages.conditions: JanSetu QA app in-app WebView, API 37 emulator 1080x2400 420dpi: A (100%) and A+ (125%) at Android font 1.0 and 2.0, plus landscape. Headless Chrome 390x844 returned HTTP 403 again (access inconclusive).

observations.issue: In JanSetu's WebView the page text stays the same size at Android font 2.0 as at 1.0; only JanSetu's own frame grows. A+ gives 125% at most.
At A+ (125%) the header shifts sideways (emblem off-centre, menu icon clipped at the edge) and the consent dialog fills about half the screen.
The site's floating '+' button overlaps the corner of 'Accept all cookies' at 100% and 125%.
Rotating the device or changing the font size recreates JanSetu's WebView and reloads the page, losing scroll position (landscape capture shows the site's loading screen).
At Android font 2.0 JanSetu's 'does not control this page' note wraps to three lines and pushes the page down.
The page shows its own accessibility and language controls; their behaviour was not tested.

pages.rationale: Text scaling is a browser-level aid that changes no page code. The defect is in JanSetu: its WebView ignores the person's Android font size. Higher sizes need reflow and consent-dialog checks because 125% already shifts the header.
pages.recommendedAction: Investigate first: start WebView text zoom from Android font scale, keep A/A+ with a clear 'original size', preserve page state across rotation, and let the frame note collapse at large font. Never restyle the consent dialog or site controls.
pages.testStatus: Emulator captures at 100%/125% and font 1.0/2.0 plus landscape; 150%/200% text zoom, TalkBack, keyboard and the full consent flow not run.
pages.limitations: One emulator and one session; Chrome 403 is not a UI finding; the site's own accessibility tools were not exercised.

history.recommendedAction: Use official controls and JanSetu guidance pending full device review; do not expand styling.

pages.reviewer: Claude Code (Phase 6A), headless Chrome screening, emulator Chrome and JanSetu in-app WebView
pages.provisionalCandidate: Existing C pilot: no measured benefit; recommend withdrawal
pages.conditions: Headless Chrome 155, 390x844 and 1280x800, one load; packaged extension/readability.css applied locally as an author stylesheet (approximation of the extension's user-origin insertion) and removed again.

observations.issue: With the stylesheet, median body text went from 16px to 16.8px and median line height from 1.69 to 1.65; no text block was under 16px before or after.
Document width 402px in a 390px viewport, unchanged by the stylesheet.
4 of 18 measured text blocks below 4.5:1 (minimum 2.13); the stylesheet does not address colour.
25 visible controls before and after; none newly covered or moved off-screen; removing the stylesheet restored identical computed styles.
No same-document hash links on /home, so in-page routing would not carry the stylesheet to unreviewed content.

pages.rationale: The pilot changes size slightly but does not address the page's measured problems (overflow, contrast) and makes line spacing marginally tighter. Applying it is not evidence of improvement.
pages.recommendedAction: Keep class D (guidance). Withdraw the Readable text pilot in the next extension release unless a revised, documented problem-specific rule set shows a measured gain.
pages.testStatus: Local before/after/restore comparison at 390px and 1280px; installed-extension, keyboard, screen-reader and route tests still pending.
pages.limitations: Author-origin approximation; one load; automated contrast ignores background images.

history.recommendedAction: Prioritize a native scholarship guide and test the site's own controls; hold any broader CSS decision until mobile, keyboard and route-change review.

pages.pageType: public guidelines with acknowledgement gate before the RTI request form
pages.reviewer: Claude Code (Phase 6A), headless Chrome screening, emulator Chrome and JanSetu in-app WebView
pages.conditions: Emulator Chrome 145 (1080x2400, 420dpi) at Android font 1.0 and 2.0; headless Chrome 155 at 390x844 with and without mobile viewport handling; read-only, no checkbox or button used.

observations.issue: No viewport meta: phones lay the page out at 980px and show it at about 0.40 scale, so 15.3px text appears at about 6px.
The acknowledgement checkbox (15x15) and Submit/Cancel (about 42x21) render at roughly 6px and 17x8px at first view.
No headings and no lang attribute; 21 numbered rules in one list.
In emulator Chrome, raising Android font to 2.0 did not visibly enlarge the page in this session.

Contains five rules a citizen needs: no Aadhaar/PAN upload, no fee below the poverty line, payment modes, wait 24-48 hours instead of paying again, and no fee for first appeal. JanSetu's own RTI record covers three of them.

pages.rationale: CSS cannot add a missing viewport meta, and the page's checkbox and Submit/Cancel begin the request and payment journey, which must stay unchanged.
pages.recommendedAction: JanSetu guidance that states all five rules with source and date, then hand off to the official page; propose the two missing rules through the editorial service workflow.
pages.testStatus: Emulator and headless observations only; no moderated task, TalkBack or keyboard test.
pages.limitations: One session; Chrome's own text-scaling setting was not changed; no request, payment or acknowledgement performed.

pages.pageType: public list of e-Sevai services with fees, documents and apply links
pages.reviewer: Claude Code (Phase 6A), headless Chrome screening, emulator Chrome and JanSetu in-app WebView
pages.provisionalCandidate: C investigation (one overflow rule) plus D
pages.conditions: Emulator Chrome 145 at Android font 1.0 and 2.0 (scroll only); headless Chrome 155 at 390x844 (desktop and mobile viewport handling) and resized to 320px/195px; read-only.

observations.issue: The 843px table of 236 services sits in div.smooth-overflow with overflow-x:hidden (and body/html also hidden), so the Fee, List of Document Required and link to apply columns start beyond a 390px screen and cannot be scrolled into view.
Median row height 203 CSS px; in emulator Chrome each service row fills most of a screen.
235 of 615 measured text blocks below 4.5:1 (minimum 3.66), mostly link text.
The site offers A-/A/A+ and a screen-reader link; enlarging text does not make clipped columns reachable.

pages.rationale: A public page with no form fields; the clipping is a single container property, so one reversible rule may restore access without restyling text or controls. JanSetu's own TN records lack fees and most documents, so guidance cannot yet replace the page.
pages.recommendedAction: Investigate the proposed overflow rule against the acceptance criteria; do not allowlist yet. In parallel, source TN fees and documents through the editorial workflow.
pages.testStatus: Static-fixture test of the rule mechanics passes; no live application of the rule, installed-extension, keyboard or screen-reader test.
pages.limitations: Columns may be reachable some other way (for example desktop width or the site's screen-reader page), which human review must check.
